title: Hierarchical prefix clustering and fast invalidation for embedding cache
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our embeddings endpoint and reranking workflows are incurring significant duplicate compute and high tail latency due to noisy prefix keys and inconsistency around document updates. Current prefix caching is conservative (exact-string prefixes) and eviction policies are coarse TTLs which cause wasted compute and stale hits for frequently edited content. This ticket proposes a hierarchical prefix clustering approach combined with content fingerprinting and a fast invalidation scheduler to increase cache hit rate, reduce 95th/99th percentile latency, and avoid serving stale embeddings after document edits.

Goals: reduce per-request embedding compute by 20-40% for reranking workloads, raise effective cache hit rate for prefix queries by +25pp on targeted customers, reduce 95th percentile embedding latency by 30% under typical batch sizes, and ensure invalidation windows for edits are bounded with <5s propagation for private/dedicated deployments.

Scope: design and implement server-side changes to the embedding cache service and the gating logic in the embeddings API. Includes: hierarchical clustering of prefixes (shingle-aware grouping), deterministic content fingerprinting (salted SHA-1 trimmed to 64 bits for storage), optimistic read-dedupe that merges coalesced requests, a TTL scheduler that supports heartbeat-based extension for hot prefixes, and an invalidation path that supports immediate and eventual modes depending on deployment tier (hosted vs. private).

Out-of-scope: client SDK changes, UI console work (those will be follow-ups), full KV-store compaction (follow-up migration ticket).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiment shows >=25% increase in cache hits for selected reranking workloads compared to baseline (A/B) over 72h
95th percentile embedding latency reduction >=30% under synthetic workload (50 qps, median sequence length 384) in staging cluster
Invalidation path ensures edited-document reads reflect new embeddings within 5s for dedicated/hosted; documented eventual-policy for on-prem deployments
No regressions observed in embedding quality (cosine similarity drift <0.5%) on benchmark datasets
Rollout plan and feature flag implemented with per-customer opt-out
technical_notes: Prefix clustering: use token-shingle sliding window to produce normalized prefix canonical forms; cluster prefixes by Hamming distance on shingle bitmaps into hierarchical buckets (hot/cold).

Content fingerprint: canonicalize whitespace and punctuation, apply tenant-specific salt + SHA-1 then truncate for 64-bit key; store full fingerprint in metadata to detect hash collisions during debugging.

Dedupe semantics: optimistic coalescing — first request triggers compute, concurrent reads to same cluster wait on shared future with a small jitter window to avoid stampede. Fall back to best-effort non-blocking read for strict latency SLOs.
TTL scheduler: adaptive TTL based on observed access recency and tenant QPS. Hot prefixes auto-extend on heartbeat up to a configurable cap. Cold prefixes decay exponentially to allow eviction.

Invalidation: two-mode invalidation API — immediate invalidation for committed writes (hosted/dedicated) that pushes keys to a fast invalidation queue (Redis stream -> cache node fanout) and eventual invalidation for offline/on-prem using tombstones with vector timestamp reconciliation.
Sharding: tag cluster fingerprints with shard id; invalidation fanout limited to affected shards to avoid cluster-wide churn.
Metrics: emit cache_hit, cache_miss, cache_eviction_reason, invalidation_latency_ms, dedupe_wait_ms, compute_saved_tokens per tenant.
Quality guardrails: run regression evals on curated prompt set (semantic drift, rank stability) before enabling wide rollout. If drift > threshold, automatically disable clustering for that tenant.

Trade-offs considered: stronger dedupe reduces compute but increases chance of staleness; we prioritize correctness for edited content by bounding invalidation latency and providing per-tenant strict mode.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal-only staging cluster, run controlled load tests and regression evals (2 weeks)
Stage 2: limited customer canary (select 3 customers with reranking workloads), monitor metrics and quality (1 week)
Stage 3: progressive rollout to hosted customers with health checks; enable by default for new tenants after 30d if stable
Stage 4: optional backport to Dedicated control plane with stricter invalidation semantics and per-tenant config UI
